overall.summary: All coverage, preservation, closed-form, claim and prose numbers reproduce, and every part behaves as described under probing; three technical statements are imprecise: an off-by-one state count, an active-row count of 304 (306), and an overstated 'the network reproduces' for the low-usage churn rates.

findings.statement: 22 inputs are unconnected (incl. totalDayCharge, totalNightCharge, totalEveCalls, totalIntlCalls, areaCode:408, 16 states)
findings.check: mapped the root's 22 unconnected input nodes to feature names on the replayed model
findings.evidence: the 22 are total intl calls, total night charge, total eve calls, total day charge, area code:408 and 17 states (9, 7, 43, 39, 34, 31, 25, 23, 22, 21, 18, 17, 15, 14, 13, 12, 10); 4 + 1 + 16 = 21 does not add up to the stated 22. Total and the named numeric inputs are right; the state count is off by one
commands: python scratch: feature_names of root entry nodes -69 ... -3 via explaneat.verify.model.load

findings.statement: active_rows: 304 (Active on 7.6% of train rows (CSC>=4), never for state:49)
findings.check: ablate the part and subgroup CSC>=4 split by West Virginia
findings.evidence: the hinge is active on 306 training rows (318 with 4+ calls minus the 12 in West Virginia), as claim C127 says; 304 does not reproduce. The 7.6% share and the never-for-state:49 statement hold (0 of 12 WV customers with 4+ calls)
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify ablate experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-9fa8f0 --part ann_92 --to zero
uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-9fa8f0 --where "`number customer service calls` >= 4"
uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-9fa8f0 --where "`number customer service calls` >= 4 and state == '49'"

findings.statement: for CSC>=4 the low-usage arm dominates (empirical churn 0.88 low-day vs 0.24 high-day, which the network reproduces)
findings.check: subgroups CSC>=4 by daytime minutes, observed vs mean predicted risk
findings.evidence: the empirical rates reproduce (CSC>=4 and day minutes <160: 88.5%, n=113; >=180.5: 24.7%, n=158), and the model ranks the two groups correctly, but it does not reproduce the levels: mean predicted risk 65.4% vs 88.5% observed for <160 (71.4% vs 94.5% for <140), and 40.8% vs 24.7% (or 22.8% for >=200) for high day use. 'Reproduces' overstates the fit by about 20 points on each arm
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-9fa8f0 --where "`number customer service calls` >= 4 and `total day minutes` < 160"

uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-9fa8f0 --where "`number customer service calls` >= 4 and `total day minutes` < 140"
